head.1: Featherview — free, open-source image viewer for Mac
page.7: Photos at the speed of
page.8: Double-click a photo, press →. Preview stays on that one photo; Featherview goes through the whole folder, about 20 ms a photo. A free, open-source image viewer for the Mac: toss the rejects, batch-convert the keepers.

firstopen.3: Drag Featherview to Applications, then paste this into Terminal once. It works on any account, administrator or not.

firstopen.6: Or install with Homebrew, which opens it straight away:
firstopen.8: Why the extra step? Featherview is made in our spare time and given away for free. For macOS to open it straight away, Apple has to notarize it, and that costs 99 € / $99 every year. So far of 99 are covered. If Featherview turns out useful to you, a contribution towards that fee would mean a lot, even $5 once, and when the fee is paid this step goes away for everyone. Thank you for trying it either way.
page.21: psst: the keys work right here. Try holding →.
preview.2: Double-click a photo, press →. Only one of them moves on.
preview.3: Preview shows the photo you opened and nothing else; to see the rest you go back to Finder, select them all and open them together. Featherview opens the whole folder with the first photo: → for the next, ← for the previous, about 20 ms each.
preview.5: Recorded on macOS 27.2 with Featherview 0.13.1. Photos: NASA, taken from the International Space Station, public domain.
speed.2: We looked for a loading spinner. There isn’t one.
speed.3: The next photo is ready before you ask for it. Huge folders open without the window freezing. You stop waiting and just look.

features.2: Everything you need to sort a folder of photos. Nothing in the way.
features.3: One window, the picture edge to edge, and your keyboard. Panels appear only when you ask.
features.5: Double-click a photo in Finder. It opens, and the rest of the folder lines up behind it.
features.7: Rotate, zoom, trash, full screen. Each is a single key, no finger yoga. Mouse fans get a toolbar.
features.9: R and L turn JPEG, HEIC and TIFF without touching a single pixel.
features.11: Delete goes to the Trash. Batch output never overwrites. One broken file never stops the show.
features.13: Press I for the histogram, the camera and exposure, and where the shot was taken, in your language and worked out on your Mac, with nothing sent anywhere.
features.15: Real Mac menus, full screen, Open With, drag and drop, true colours, and HDR that glows on HDR screens.
keyboard.2: Your mouse can take the day off.
keyboard.3: Every viewer action is one key, no modifiers to hold. Coming from a classic Windows viewer? Your fingers already know most of these. The ⌘ shortcuts are there too.
keyboard.8: Next, then on to the next folder
keyboard.15: Turn it the right way up
keyboard.16: Move or copy to a favourite folder
keyboard.19: // Esc leaves full screen. It never, ever quits.
formats.2: Opens the usual suspects. And the odd ones.
formats.3: Every picture shows up the right way round, in true colour.
formats.5: Phone photos, camera RAW, the modern web formats WebP, AVIF and JPEG XL, even SVG and PDF pages.
formats.21: Formats macOS gave up on, read by Featherview itself. That PCX from your first PC, a MacPaint doodle, a telescope’s FITS? Opens fine, and Finder shows their thumbnails and Quick Look previews too.
formats.35: Layered Photoshop PSD and PSB, GIMP, Krita, Paint.NET and PaintShop Pro files, shown flattened. Procreate artwork from your iPad too, at full size. No editor needed.
formats.44: And it saves to all the useful ones: JPEG, PNG, HEIC, AVIF, WebP, JPEG XL, TIFF, PDF, and even ICO and ICNS for the icon crowd.
batch.2: A whole shoot in. Exactly what you need out.
batch.3: Pick the keepers, choose a format, a size and a name, add the steps you want, watch the preview follow along, press Convert. Keep the recipe as a preset for next time.
batch.4: Never overwrites a file<small>Your originals stay exactly as they were.</small>
batch.5: Keeps the story<small>Camera details and location come along.</small>
batch.6: Doesn’t give up<small>A file it can’t read is skipped. The rest still gets done.</small>
batch.7: Resize, crop, rotate, fix colour, sharpen, add a border, stamp text or a watermark, and rename with a pattern.
languages.2: Speaks your language. Thirty of them.
languages.3: Featherview follows your Mac’s language. Arabic and Hebrew flip the whole window right to left. Your photos stay the right way round.
faq.4: No, it runs on Windows only. Featherview is an independent Mac alternative in the same spirit: open one picture and the arrow keys take you through the folder, R and L rotate, and batch conversion handles the rest. Most of the single keys are the same, so your fingers already know them. It isn’t affiliated with IrfanView.
faq.5: How do I open a PSD without Photoshop?
faq.6: Double-click it in Featherview. Layered PSD and PSB files show flattened, even 4.6 GB ones, and Finder shows thumbnails of GIMP and Procreate files too.
faq.7: Can I view WebP and JPEG XL on a Mac?
faq.8: Yes, and save to them too: WebP, JPEG XL, AVIF and HEIC, plus older formats macOS no longer opens, with Quick Look previews in Finder.
faq.9: Can I flip through a folder like on Windows?
faq.10: That’s the point. Open one photo, then → and ← step through the whole folder. Delete moves a reject to the Trash.
faq.11: Can it batch convert and resize?
faq.12: Yes: HEIC to JPEG, PNG to WebP, resize, rename, crop and watermark a whole shoot, with a live preview. It never overwrites a file.
faq.14: Yes. Open source under the MIT licence, no ads, no account, no paid tier. It updates itself, and runs on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs with macOS 14 or later.
page.22: Free, light as a feather, made for the Mac.
page.23: Written in Swift on macOS’s own image engine. Your Photos library too, browsed with the arrow keys. Next up.
page.26: An independent Mac alternative to IrfanView, not affiliated with it or its author. Thanks to Irfan Škiljan, whose viewer has shown for decades how fast looking at images can be.
head.2@content: Featherview is a free, open-source image viewer for Mac and an independent alternative to IrfanView. Flip through a folder with the arrow keys, open WebP, JPEG XL, HEIC, RAW and PSD files, and batch-convert.
